dialect.detail: Likely RM-COBOL or similar PC-based COBOL (IBM-PC SOURCE/OBJECT-COMPUTER, VALUE OF FILE-ID, INDEXED file with ASSIGN TO DISK). Greek-language comments and identifiers suggest a Greek academic environment, possibly using a DOS-era PC COBOL compiler.

purpose.domain_detail: Greek university student records system; program creates/initializes an indexed student file (MHTRMA = student registry)
purpose.summary: This subprogram opens and initializes an indexed student registry file (MHTRWA.DAT). It accepts a student ID and name via LINKAGE SECTION, writes a record to the file, and displays a Greek confirmation message upon completion.

notable_features: LINKAGE SECTION with PROCEDURE DIVISION USING (subprogram interface)
INDEXED file organization with RECORD KEY
VALUE OF FILE-ID clause (older PC COBOL style)
Greek-language identifiers and comments (EPWN, ONOM, MHTRMA, etc.)
Mixed line numbering: some lines have 000000 sequence numbers, others are blank (inconsistent)
OPEN INPUT then CLOSE then OPEN OUTPUT pattern (unusual double open)
verdict.notes: The file has inconsistent sequence numbers (some lines have 000000, others have no sequence number at all), suggesting manual editing or mixing of sources. The Greek identifiers and comments strongly suggest a Greek university exercise. The dialect is ambiguous between RM-COBOL and Micro Focus PC COBOL given the IBM-PC computer names and VALUE OF FILE-ID syntax; RM-COBOL is a reasonable guess for this era and style.
